newsitem.title: USA: US CFTC extends comment time for rule review plan.
newsitem.headline: US CFTC extends comment time for rule review plan.

text.p: U.S. futures regulators said they agreed to extend the public comment period on a plan that would allow certain exchange rules to take effect without regulatory approval.

In a notice in the Federal Register, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said interested parties now have until January 31 to file comments on the proposal, part of the agency's ongoing effort to streamline its rule review process.
A CFTC spokesman said the extension was granted after parties said they needed more time to respond to the plan, which applies to rules that do not involve contract terms.
The agency's proposal would alter the review process so that certain rule changes generally could be deemed approved or become effective without commission approval.
The review period could be lengthened if the CFTC sought more time to consider a proposed rule.
Futures industry officials and exchange leaders have long maintained that lengthy U.S. regulatory reviews pose a threat to their business.
